The search didn't turn up a single GitHub issue that matches your query exactly. It did return several facebook/react issues and related reports about hydration mismatches caused by browser extensions or injected markup.

- **Most recent (React 19.2.4):** Issue #36169, opened March 2026, reports hydration errors from a `<script defer>` in `<head>`. The reporter says an extension can also cause this kind of mismatch by altering the HTML before React loads. It can also happen if the client has a browser extension installed which messes with the HTML before React loaded.
- **React 18 devtools case:** Issue #25924 describes a script injected by the React DevTools extension triggering a mismatch. It is still marked unconfirmed.
- **Plugin-injected script:** Issue #24430 (React 18) covers a plugin inserting a script tag before `<head>`, which causes a mismatch. It's in the Backlog.
- **React's stated position:** A Video Speed Controller issue (igrigorik/videospeed #1255) cites the React 19 release post. It says the team expects extensions to mostly avoid unexpected HTML, but tags in `<head>` and `<body>` are skipped in React 19. If React needs to re-render the entire document due to an unrelated hydration mismatch, it will leave in place stylesheets inserted by third-party scripts and browser extensions.
- **Workaround example:** Next.js discussion #72035 traces a Next.js 15 / React 19 hydration error to the ColorZilla extension adding a `cz-shortcut-listen` attribute to `<body>`. One user shared a fix that removes the attribute before hydration and uses a MutationObserver to stop it returning.
- **Unrelated React 19 bugs:** Issues #32975 and #33133 involve `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` combined with `suppressHydrationWarning`, not extensions. #33133 was closed as not planned.

The most relevant results are #36169 (recent, React 19) and #25924 (extensions, React 18). The Next.js discussion is the best source for a practical workaround.

content.text:
There's no single canonical issue for this. A few related ones do exist.

**Closest matches in `facebook/react`:**
- [#25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924): "Scripts injected by browser extensions (e.g. React dev tools) may cause hydration errors." It was filed against React 18 and is still marked unconfirmed. It's the most direct issue about extensions causing mismatches.
- [#36169](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/36169): a hydration mismatch on `<script defer>` in `<head>` (React 19.2.4, opened March 2026). The reporter notes that an extension altering the HTML before React loads can cause the same kind of mismatch.
- [#24430](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/24430): a plugin injects a script tag at the top, causing a mismatch (React 18, in the Backlog).

**React 19-specific:**
- [Next.js discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035): a Next.js 15 / React 19 hydration error caused by the ColorZilla extension adding a `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute to `<body>`. It includes a workaround that removes the attribute before hydration.
- [igrigorik/videospeed #1255](https://github.com/igrigorik/videospeed/issues/1255): the Video Speed Controller extension's issue cites the React 19 release notes. React 19 skips unexpected tags in `<head>` and `<body>`, and it leaves third-party stylesheets in place if it has to re-render the whole document.

I haven't opened these pages, so the details come from the search snippets. I'd start with #25924 for the underlying problem and the Next.js discussion for a workaround.
